$comment: Accepted vulnerability findings (p7-supply-chain, docs/security/dependency-policy.md §5). Every entry: id (advisory id or alias), optional package, reason (why not exploitable here / why no fix), owner, expires (YYYY-MM-DD, at most 90 days ahead). Expired entries fail the gate.

entries.reason: high: Agent drops a function-valued tls option (custom checkServerIdentity) through a JSON clone. Not exploitable here: pi builds its global EnvHttpProxyAgent with only connect.autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout and no tls callback (dist/core/http-dispatcher.js of 1.4.0), so Node's default chain and hostname checks still apply. The pi runtime pin @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 depends on undici 8.10.2 exactly (no range), so neither a lockfile refresh nor our workspace can move it without overriding the contract-tested runtime tree. Fixed upstream: pi-coding-agent 1.5.0 and later depend on undici 8.12.3 or newer (1.6.0: 8.12.4). Fix: promote the pi runtime pin through the runtime update path (canary worker first, dependency-policy.md section 3).

high: cache poisoning when an originless Agent composes redirect() and a shared cache(). Not exploitable here: pi 1.4.0 composes no cache interceptor (its dispatcher is a plain EnvHttpProxyAgent). The pi runtime pin @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 depends on undici 8.10.2 exactly (no range), so neither a lockfile refresh nor our workspace can move it without overriding the contract-tested runtime tree. Fixed upstream: pi-coding-agent 1.5.0 and later depend on undici 8.12.3 or newer (1.6.0: 8.12.4). Fix: promote the pi runtime pin through the runtime update path (canary worker first, dependency-policy.md section 3).

high: a TLS 1.2 server that renegotiates with a non-matching certificate crashes the client process. Reachable: pi sends its provider requests through undici. Impact: a malicious or compromised HTTPS endpoint the job talks to can end that pi job's process (availability of one job; no data exposure). moderate: CPU denial of service through globparts amplification of a crafted pattern. No 10.x fix exists (fixed in 11.0.1). Workspace: dev-only, pulled in by eslint 10.12.0 and typescript-eslint 8.71.2 with patterns from our own lint config. pi runtime: pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 depends on minimatch 10.2.6 exactly and matches the model selector and package filters, which our adapter sets, not untrusted input. Fix: eslint 10.15.0 + typescript-eslint >= 8.73.0 (minimatch 11; needs a full lint run) and the pi pin promotion (pi-coding-agent 1.6.0 uses minimatch 11.0.3).

moderate: backslash in the request path is treated as a separator, bypassing proxy path rules. Not reachable here: hono and @hono/node-server come in through @modelcontextprotocol/sdk under the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.310, and the SDK imports only server/mcp.js and the zod-compat modules, whose import graph loads neither hono nor @hono/node-server (checked against the 1.32.x dist); no HTTP server of the MCP SDK is started in the claude-code runtime. Fix available within the declared ranges (hono >= 4.13.16, @hono/node-server >= 2.1.6): refresh infra/worker/images/claude-code/package-lock.json at the next claude-code runtime update (dependency-policy.md section 3; canary worker first).
